household: with Justin, Max, Jerry and Theresa Russo
creator: Todd J. Greenwald
address_as_given: 5102 Waverly Place, in an apartment above the family's Waverly Sub Station
notes: The family lives above its sandwich shop. Waverly Place numbers run only into the low hundreds, so 5102 does not exist; placed on Waverly Place near Sixth Avenue. The number comes from the show's fan wiki; the show was taped in Los Angeles.
source_quote: The Waverly Sub Station is a deli restaurant situated at 5102 Waverly Place in the borough of Manhattan in New York's Greenwich Village neighborhood.
source2_quote: Alex, Justin, and Max Russo are three teenage wizards-in-training living in an apartment on Waverly Place in Greenwich Village, Manhattan, New York City.

household: nanny to Emma, Luke, Ravi and Zuri Ross, with butler Bertram
creator: Pamela Eells O'Connell
address_as_given: penthouse of The Fairfield, Upper West Side
notes: The Fairfield is a fictional building; no street is given. Placed at the Upper West Side centroid. Taped in Los Angeles; no real exterior identified.
source_quote: She accepts a job as a nanny and moves into a multimillion-dollar penthouse on the Upper West Side, Manhattan with the wealthy Ross family.
source2_quote: The Ross Family Penthouse is a luxury 20 million dollar penthouse of The Fairfield, a luxurious hotel located on the Upper West Side of Manhattan.

creator: Fred Barron, Dottie Dartland, Marco Pennette
notes: Scouting NY names 168 Duane Street only in passing; we could not confirm whether the show states this address or used the building as an exterior. 168 Duane is a real 1880s Tribeca building. The show was taped in Los Angeles.
source_quote: or should I have included Caroline in the City’s 168 Duane Street apartment building?
source2_quote: It stars Lea Thompson as cartoonist Caroline Duffy, who lives in Manhattan.

household: with Sid
creator: Isaac Aptaker, Elizabeth Berger
address_as_given: Ted and Marshall's old apartment, above MacLaren's
geocode_query: West 75th Street and Amsterdam Avenue, Manhattan
notes: The spinoff puts Jesse and Sid in the How I Met Your Mother apartment; the 75th and Amsterdam corner comes from the parent show, which never gave a street number. Exteriors were not shot in New York.
source_quote: He lives with Sid in Ted and Marshall's old apartment.
source2_quote: Ted Mosby's apartment was located on the Upper West Side of New York City, at 75th and Amsterdam.

household: with Jemaine Clement
creator: James Bobin, Jemaine Clement, Bret McKenzie
address_as_given: their apartment, shot on location at 28 Henry Street
notes: The show gives no address; it shot the apartment exterior on location, and fans place it at 28 Henry Street. One page of the same fan site says 227 Henry Street and another mentions 37 Henry Street, so the number is not certain. Bret and Jemaine play fictional versions of themselves.
source_quote: Sally walks Jemaine home to the apartment at 28 Henry Street.
source2_quote: He is often seen involved performing maintenance in the building and in Bret and Jemaine's apartment.

household: with Jemaine Clement
creator: James Bobin, Jemaine Clement, Bret McKenzie
notes: Location exterior per a fan-compiled filming-locations site. Fan comments disagree on whether the original building still stands.
source_quote: Apartment building at 28 Henry Street.

creator: Bob Ellison, Peter Noah (from John Sullivan's British series)
address_as_given: an apartment in Rego Park, Queens
notes: The story puts John in Rego Park, but the exterior used is in Astoria; he later moves to a second exterior at 28-28 29th Street, Astoria.
source_quote: When the court grants Wendy the house and custody of their son, Matthew, John moves into an apartment in the Rego Park neighborhood of Queens.

creator: Bob Ellison, Peter Noah (from John Sullivan's British series)
notes: First exterior. The later apartment exterior is 28-28 29th Street, Astoria.
source_quote: The building is actually 27-56 27 Street in Astoria, Queens. When he later moves, he moves one street away to 28-28 29 Street, also in Astoria, Queens.

household: with her sister Eileen
creator: based on Ruth McKenney's stories
address_as_given: a Greenwich Village brownstone owned by Mr. Appopoplous
notes: The 1960-61 CBS sitcom version. The source stories and play put the sisters in a Christopher Street basement; the TV page gives only Greenwich Village.
source_quote: The two women find an apartment in a Greenwich Village brownstone owned by Mr. Appopoplous and befriend reporter Chick Adams.

household: with husband Andy and their children
creator: Jill Kargman
notes: Jill Weber is Jill Kargman playing a fictionalized version of herself; no street is given.
source_quote: The series focuses on Jill Kargman playing a fictionalized version of herself, Jill Weber, who is forced to navigate the clique of wealthy mothers who reside in New York's prestigious Upper East Side.

household: and her friends Tye, Quinn and Angie
creator: Tracy Oliver
notes: The four friends live in Harlem; no specific apartments are given in the source.
source_quote: The series follows four female friends who met while attending New York University and are now in their thirties, living in Harlem, as they try to balance love, life, and their careers as working professionals.

household: with his wife Ruth
creator: Dennis Klein (developed from One Foot in the Grave)
address_as_given: the corner of 33rd Avenue and 1539 Blake Street, Astoria
notes: There is no Blake Street in Astoria (Blake Avenue is in Brooklyn), so the corner is impossible; placed along 33rd Avenue in Astoria. Interiors were shot at Kaufman Astoria Studios.
source_quote: Set at the corner of 33rd Avenue and 1539 Blake Street in Astoria, Queens, the show starred Cosby as Hilton Lucas

household: with Joey Harris and Michael Taylor; Judge Wilbur is the landlady
creator: Michael Jacobs, Danielle Alexandra
address_as_given: Joey's loft, above the building's cafe
notes: SoHo is our inference from the title of the episode in which the family settles on Joey's loft. A Wikipedia mirror names 484 Broome Street as the exterior, but we could not fetch a page that says so.
source_quote: They opt to live in Joey's hip loft.

household: with Owen, Paige and Cole Tillerman
creator: Loren Bouchard, Nora Smith, Josh Gad
notes: Animated. Owen is the park manager and the family lives in the castle. Edendale Castle does not exist; the fan wiki suggests it stands in for Belvedere Castle, where it is placed. The show does not pin it to a spot in the park.
source_quote: the musical series tells the story of the Tillerman–Hunter family who live in Edendale Castle in Central Park.
source2_quote: Despite the show being set in a real location, "Edendale Castle" does not actually exist in the real Central Park.

household: with Marty the zebra, Melman the giraffe and Gloria the hippo
creator: Eric Darnell, Tom McGrath
geocode_query: East 64th Street and Fifth Avenue, Manhattan
notes: Animated. The real Central Park Zoo has no lions, giraffes or hippos; the film's zoo is a fictionalized version.
source_quote: In New York City, a lion named Alex lives in the Central Park Zoo as a star attraction known as the "King of New York"
source2_quote: Central Park Zoo, Central Park, Manhattan.

household: with Kowalski, Rico and Private
creator: Mark McCorkle, Bob Schooley
address_as_given: the penguin habitat, Central Park Zoo
geocode_query: East 64th Street and Fifth Avenue, Manhattan
notes: Animated spinoff of Madagascar; the penguins live in the zoo's penguin habitat.
source_quote: This is the penguins' headquarters and home. There are currently four penguins residing here (Skipper, Kowalski, Rico, and Private).

household: with Oliver, Georgette and the butler Winston
creator: George Scribner (director)
notes: Animated. The number comes from the Disney fan wiki; we could not confirm it is shown on screen. The film's house is a freestanding mansion, unlike the real building at that number.
source_quote: The building is located at #1125, 5th Avenue, New York, on the corner of 5th Avenue and a cross street.

household: with Dodger, Rita, Tito, Francis and Einstein; briefly Oliver
creator: George Scribner (director)
address_as_given: a barge at the city docks
neighborhood: East River waterfront near the Brooklyn Bridge
notes: Animated. The film gives no pier. The fan wiki puts Sykes's warehouse at the same docks next to the Brooklyn Bridge; placed at the Manhattan foot of the bridge, though the Brooklyn shore is possible.
source_quote: Dom DeLuise as Fagin, a lowly but well-meaning thief who lives on a barge with his dogs.
source2_quote: The building is located somewhere in the City Docks, next to the Brooklyn Bridge in New York.

household: with Papa, Mama, Tanya and Yasha Mousekewitz
creator: Don Bluth (director)
address_as_given: the family's new tailoring shop and home, Lower East Side
notes: Animated. The family lives above a human sweatshop; the film shows Hester Street but gives no address. Placed near Hester Street.
source_quote: They found him, finally, in a slum on New York’s Lower East Side. It’s 1886.
source2_quote: Fievel is cast into slavery in a sweatshop run by a fat rat named Moe (that, ironically, is a short distance below his family's new tailoring shop/home).

household: with his owner Katie and Duke
creator: Chris Renaud (director)
notes: Animated. The film names no street; the fan wiki places the building in Little Italy from rooftop views of the Manhattan Bridge.
source_quote: The Apartment Building is the central setting of The Secret Life of Pets, situated in Little Italy, New York City.
source2_quote: A Jack Russell Terrier named Max lives with his owner Katie in a New York City apartment.

household: with Benny the Ball, Brain, Choo-Choo, Fancy-Fancy and Spook
creator: William Hanna, Joseph Barbera
notes: Animated. Hoagy's Alley is fictional and the show gives no neighborhood; the marker sits in Midtown only to put it in Manhattan.
source_quote: The title character, Top Cat (T.C.), is the leader of a gang of Manhattan alley cats living in Hoagy's Alley

household: with her cat Cagney
creator: Greg Weisman
notes: Animated. SoHo comes from the first-season series bible, not the episodes. The gargoyles' own homes (atop the fictional Eyrie Building and a precinct clock tower) have no real location.
source_quote: The location of Elisa's loft being in SoHo was revealed in the Series Bible for the first season of the show.

household: with Ray Stantz, Egon Spengler, Winston Zeddemore and Slimer
creator: DiC / Columbia Pictures Television (from the 1984 film)
notes: Animated. Unlike in the film, the team lives in the firehouse, sleeping on the third floor. Ince Boulevard is a Culver City street by the Sony lot, not in New York. Placed, by our inference, at the film's firehouse (Hook & Ladder 8).
source_quote: Address: 3960 Ince Boulevard New York, New York
source2_quote: All the Ghostbusters sleep in separate beds.
